1.w: And these three men ceased from answering Job, because he [was] righteous in his own eyes.

2.w: But the anger of Elihu son of Barachel, the Buzite from the family of Ram, was kindled; his anger was kindled against Job, upon his justifying himself rather than God.

3.w: And his anger was kindled against his three friends, upon that they had not found an answer, and they had declared Job wrong.

4.w: And Elihu had waited with words [to] Job, because they [were] older than he in days.

5.w: And Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of the three men, and his anger was kindled.

6.w: And Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said, “I [am] Young in days, and you⁺ [are] aged; upon thus I shrank back, and I was afraid of declaring my knowledge to you⁺.

7.w: I said, “Days shall speak, and a multitude of years shall make known wisdom.’

8.w: Surely it [is] a spirit in a man, and the breath of Shaddai gives them understanding.

9.w: Not [only] the great [in years] [are] wise, nor do [only] the aged understand justice.

10.w: Therefore I say, ‘Listen to me; I will declare my knowledge, even I.’

11.w: Behold, I have waited for your⁺ words; I gave [my] ear to your⁺ reasonings, while you⁺ searched for the words.

12.w: And to you⁺ I attended, and behold, there was no one proving Job wrong [or] answering his words among you⁺,

13.w: lest you⁺ say, ‘We have found wisdom; let God drive him away, not man.’

14.w: And he has not arrayed [his] words toward me, and I will not answer him with your⁺ words.

15.w: They are dismayed, [and] do not answer anymore; the words have gone away from them.

16.w: And I have waited, because they do not speak, because they stand there [and] do not answer anymore?

17.w: I will answer—even I—my portion; I will show my knowledge—even I.

18.w: For I am full of words; the spirit [in] my belly presses me.

19.w: Behold, my belly [is] like wine not opened; like new wineskins, it is bursting open.

20.w: I will speak, and there is refreshment for me; I will open my lips and answer.

21.w: Do not, please, let me lift up the face of a man; and do not let me give a title to man.

22.w: For I do not know how to give a title; soon my Maker would take me away.
